texts.preamble: Sakina vs The State Of Telangana on 25 September, 2024 Author: P.Sam Koshy Bench: P.Sam Koshy, G.Radha Rani The Hon'Ble Sri Justice P.Sam Koshy And The Hon'Ble Dr. Justice G. Radha Rani Writ Petition No.23925 of 2024 Order:
texts.facts: The writ petition is one which has been filed seeking for issuance of a Writ in the nature of Habeas Corpus with a prayer for production of the detenu before the Court and quashment of the aforementioned orders. 4. Brief facts of the case are that detenu has committed an offence of Dacoit under Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities Act, 1986 across various Police Station limits but the police authorities had detained the detenu on 03.06.2024 under multiple cases. The detenu and his associates allegedly used a female accomplice to lure victims and then demanded money under threat. In the first case, viz., Cr.No.23 of 2023 of Asifnagar Police Station, the detenu and his associates allegedly extorted Rs.2,50,000/- from a catering business owner under the pretext of taking a selfie with one of the accused's wife. The second case Cr.No.32 of 2023 of Musheerabad Police Station, the detenu and his associates again involved in extorting Rs.9,80,000/- from a rice Sakina vs The State Of Telangana on 25 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168717843/ 1 business owner through similar tactics . The third case, viz., Cr.No.6 of 2023 of Santoshnagar Police Station, where the detenu and his associates allegedly lured a catering business owner of an hotel and extorted Rs.47,000/- while threatening to circulate compromising photographs and videos. 5. The detenu was arrested, granted bail and released in 09.05.2023 for the above cases. However, the detention order was ::3:: PSK,J & Dr.GRR,J wp_23925_2024 passed shortly after his release on 03.06.2023 and subsequently, the detenu was detained again on 18.10.2023 in connection with Cr.No.32 of 2023 of Musheerabad Police Station and was released on 27.01.2024. Thereafter, the detenu was arrested on 21.08.2023 in relation to Cr.No.06 of 2023 of Santoshnagar Police Station and released on 27.02.2024. Despite the detention order being in force during these periods of judicial custody, it was only executed against the detenu on 12.08.2024 after his release from jail in February, 2024.
texts.arguments: 6. Learned counsel for the petitioner further contended that the detention order is based on stale crimes that were committed by the detenu in the year 2022 but were only registered on 13.01.2023. This significant gap between the alleged incidents and the registration of crimes undermines the necessity of preventive detention. He further contended that these crimes primarily affected law and order rather public order, and that the use of preventive detention laws should be reserved for the rarest of rare cases that pose a threat to public order and not as a substitute for the ordinary criminal justice system. ::4 : : Furthermore, learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the documents allegedly served to the detenu in English despite his known language being Urdu, impaired the detenu's constitutional right under Article 22(5) to make representations against the detention order. Moreover, he alleges that the material relied on for the detention was not supplied to the detenu within the mandated period of five (05) days from the date of his detention which violated the detenu's rights. 8. Lastly, the learned counsel for the petitioner contended that despite the detention order being in force, the impugned order was not executed while the detenu was in judicial custody for subsequent arrest related to the same cases. Instead, it was enforced months after his release from these subsequent arrests. Such discretionary enforcement of preventive detention laws amount to taking law into their own hands and punishing citizens outside the bounds of the regular criminal justice system. Thus, the impugned order of preventive detention is liable to be set-aside and the detenu to be set free. 9. Per contra, learned Special Government Pleader argued that the detenu had been habitually committing dacoities by trapping victims in honey-traps along with his associates in an organized Sakina vs The State Of Telangana on 25 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168717843/ 2 manner within the limits of different Police Station of Hyderabad Police Commissionerate. Further, the detenu has been involved in unlawful acts and illegal activities which disturb public order as well as peace and tranquility in the society. All these specific cases for which he has been charged are cases which are otherwise subjected to trial for the offences punishable under the provisions of Indian Penal Code and cannot be generalized and brought within the purview of public order." In the said judgment, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in paragraph Nos.23, 24 and 25 dealing with the explanation attached to Section 2(a) has held as under: "23. The explanation attached to Section 2(a) of the Act 1986 reproduced above contemplates that 'public order' shall be deemed to have been affected adversely or shall be deemed likely to be affected adversely, inter alia if any of the activities of any person referred to in Section 2(a) directly or indirectly, are causing or is likely to cause any harm, danger or alarm or feeling of insecurity among the general public or any section thereof or a grave or widespread danger to life, property or public health. The Explanation to Section 2(a) also provides that for the purpose of Section 2, a person shall be deemed to be "acting in any manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order" when such person is a "GOONDA" and engaged in activities which affect adversely or are likely to affect adversely the maintenance of public order. Sakina vs The State Of Telangana on 25 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168717843/ 3 24. The essential concept of preventive detention is that the detention of a person is not to punish him for something he has done but to prevent him from doing it. The basis of detention is the satisfaction of the executive about the likelihood of the detenu acting in a manner, similar to his past acts, which is likely to affect adversely the maintenance of public order and, thereby prevent him, by an order of detention, from doing the same. In one case a person is punished on proof of his guilt, and the standard is proof beyond the reasonable doubt, whereas in the other a person is detained with a view to prevent him from doing such act(s) as may be specified in the Act authorizing preventive detention. (See :HaradhanSaha v. The State of W.B., 1974 Cri LJ 1479]" ::8:: PSK,J & Dr.GRR,J wp_23925_2024 12. Again in paragraph No.32, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has in great detail dealt with the expression law and order and public order and held as under: "32. The crucial issue is whether the activities of the detenu were prejudicial to public order. While the expression 'law and order' is wider in scope inasmuch as contravention of law always affects order, 'Public order' has a narrower ambit, and could be affected by only such contravention, which affects the community or the public at large. Public order is the even tempo of life of the community taking the country as a whole or even a specified locality. It is the potentiality of the act to disturb the even tempo of life of the community which makes it prejudicial to the maintenance of the public order. In other words, the true distinction between the areas of law and order and public order lies not merely in the nature or quality of the act, but in the degree and extent Sakina vs The State Of Telangana on 25 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168717843/ 4 of its reach upon society. Acts similar in nature, but committed in different contexts and circumstances, might cause different reactions. In one case it might affect specific individuals only, and therefore touches the problem of law and order only, while in another it might affect public order. In its quality it may not differ from other similar acts, but in its potentiality, that is, in its impact on society, it may be very different. [See: Union of India v. Amrit Lal Manchanda, (2004) 3 SCC 75.]" 13. In yet another land mark decision in Ameena Begum vs. The State of Telangana, a judgment which has been pronounced under the ::9:: PSK,J & Dr.GRR,J wp_23925_2024 same provision of law, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held at paragraph Nos.34 to 37 as under: "34. In KusoSah vs. The State of Bihar , Hon'ble Y.V. Chandrachud, J. (as the Chief Justice then was) speaking for the Bench held that: "4.*** The two concepts have well defined contours, it being well established that stray and un-organised crimes of theft and assault are not matters of public order since they do not tend to affect the even flow of public life. Infractions of law are bound in some measure to lead to disorder but every infraction of law does not necessarily result in public disorder. ** * 6. ** * The power to detain a person without the safeguard of a court trial is too drastic to permit a lenient construction and therefore Courts must be astute to ensure that the detaining authority does not transgress the limitations subject to which alone the power can be exercised. ** *" (underlining ours, for emphasis) 35. Turning our attention to section 3(1) of the Act, the Government has to arrive at a subjective satisfaction that a goonda (as in the present case) has to be detained, in order to prevent him from acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order. An order of detention under section 3(1) of the Act can only be issued against a detenu to prevent him "from acting in any manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order". "Public order" is defined in the Explanation to section 2(a) of the Act as encompassing situations that cause "harm, danger or alarm or a feeling of insecurity among the general public or any section thereof or a grave wide-spread danger to life or public health". Ram Manohar Lohia (supra) is an authority to rely upon for the proposition that if liberty of an individual can be invaded under statutory rules by the simple process of making of a certain order, Sakina vs The State Of Telangana on 25 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168717843/ 5 he can Strict compliance with the letter of the rule, in such a case, has to be the essence of the matter since the statute has the potentiality to interfere with the personal liberty of an individual and a Court is precluded from going behind its face. It is said in paragraph 30 that: "30.
